title: Schur stability conjecture for image reconstruction operators
statement:
Let $W$ be a primitive stochastic matrix, let $B$ be a positive semidefinite matrix satisfying

$$
Be \leqslant \varrho(B)e
$$

and

$$
\pi^\top Be>0,
$$

where $\pi$ is the left Perron eigenvector of $W$. Define

$$
P(t)=W(I-tB),\qquad R(t)=I-W+(I+tB)^{-1}(2W-I).
$$

**Schur stability conjecture.** The operators $P(t)$ and $R(t)$ are stable, meaning that

$$
\varrho(P(t))<1\quad\text{and}\quad\varrho(R(t))<1,
$$

for all $0<t<2/\varrho(B)$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06715

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).
source_name: Debraj Banerjee and Kunal Narayan Chaudhury, “On the Schur Stability of Some Image Reconstruction Operators”, arXiv:2509.06715 (2025).

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: An unverified posted calculation claims that explicit two-dimensional examples disprove both stability assertions, while the published paper only proves stability for sufficiently small steps and selected cases.
progress.summary:
Banerjee and Chaudhury posed the conjecture in September 2025: under the stated hypotheses, both reconstruction operators should remain stable throughout the prescribed step-size interval.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06715)*

**Known results**

- Banerjee–Chaudhury (2025): both operators are stable for each sufficiently small $t>0$, although the proof gives no uniform estimate for the threshold.
- Banerjee–Chaudhury (2025): explicit stability ranges are obtained for particular classes of $W$ and $B$.
- Banerjee–Chaudhury (2025): the bound $Be\leqslant\varrho(B)e$ is shown necessary for the conjectured formulation; numerical examples indicate that the bound for $R(t)$ need not be sharp.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06715v1)*

**Posted attempt**

An unverified calculation claims that a positive-definite $2\times2$ matrix $B$ and primitive stochastic $2\times2$ matrices satisfy all hypotheses while both operators have spectral radius greater than $1$ at $t=4/5$. It further claims a parameterized family with instability for arbitrarily small positive $t$, which would refute both assertions rather than merely prove partial progress. The calculation has not been independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): the local and selected special-case results are established, while the general conjecture is now accompanied by an unverified claimed counterexample and is not mathematically settled.

*Caveats. The claimed counterexample appears only in an unverified reader-written attempt, so it cannot yet be treated as a disproof.*

solutions.body:
**Counterexample to both stability assertions, with arbitrarily small instability thresholds.**

Conjecture 1.1 of Banerjee and Chaudhury, arXiv:2509.06715, considers
\[
P(t)=W(I-tB),\qquad
R(t)=I-W+(I+tB)^{-1}(2W-I),
\]
where \(W\) is primitive and row-stochastic, \(B\) is positive semidefinite, \(e=(1,\ldots,1)^\top\), and the normalized left Perron vector \(\pi\) satisfies
\[
Be\le \rho(B)e,\qquad \pi^\top Be>0.
\]
It asserts that both spectral radii are strictly less than one throughout \(0<t<2/\rho(B)\). The conjecture does not require \(B\) to be entrywise nonnegative: the preceding discussion explicitly says that nonnegativity is not essential, and Example 1.2 includes negative off-diagonal entries.

Take
\[
W=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\7/30&23/30\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B=\frac1{11}\begin{pmatrix}9&-4\\-4&3\end{pmatrix},
\qquad t=\frac45.
\]
Indeed,
\[
W^2=
\begin{pmatrix}7/30&23/30\\161/900&739/900\end{pmatrix}>0,
\]
so \(W\) is primitive. Furthermore,
\[
\sigma(B)=\left\{1,\frac1{11}\right\},\qquad
\rho(B)=1,\qquad
Be=\frac1{11}\binom5{-1}\le\binom11.
\]
Thus \(B\) is even positive definite. The stationary vector is
\[
\pi=\frac1{37}\binom7{30},
\qquad
\pi^\top Be=\frac5{407}>0,
\]
and \(0<4/5<2/\rho(B)=2\).

Exact rational calculation gives
\[
P(4/5)=
\begin{pmatrix}
16/55&43/55\\
167/550&367/550
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
R(4/5)=
\begin{pmatrix}
700/1593&545/1593\\
253/15930&15797/15930
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Nevertheless,
\[
\det(I-P(4/5))=-\frac2{1375}<0,
\qquad
\det(I-R(4/5))=-\frac2{2655}<0.
\]
For each real two-by-two matrix \(M\), its monic characteristic polynomial therefore has \(\chi_M(1)<0\) and \(\chi_M(x)\to+\infty\) as \(x\to+\infty\). Each matrix consequently has a real eigenvalue strictly greater than one:
\[
\rho(P(4/5))>1,\qquad \rho(R(4/5))>1.
\]
Hence both claimed stability assertions fail simultaneously.

In fact the obstruction occurs arbitrarily close to zero. Keep the same positive definite \(B\), choose any \(0<s<2\), and put
\[
v=\frac1{5-s},\qquad
W_s=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\v&1-v\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\pi_s=\frac1{1+v}\binom v1.
\]
Then \(W_s\) is primitive and stochastic, \(Be\le e\), and
\[
\pi_s^\top Be=\frac{s}{11(6-s)}>0.
\]
Direct symbolic calculation yields
\[
\det(I-P_s(t))
=-\frac{t(t-s)}{11(5-s)},
\qquad
\det(I-R_s(t))
=-\frac{t(t-s)}{(5-s)(t+1)(t+11)}.
\]
At \(t=s\), both operators already have eigenvalue one, and for every \(s<t<2\), both have a real eigenvalue greater than one. Since \(s\) can be arbitrarily small while \(\rho(B)=1\) remains fixed, no positive stability threshold depending only on \(\rho(B)\) and the dimension is valid under the conjectured assumptions. The paper's separate local per-instance stability theorem remains unaffected.
